- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth 3-day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict in early periods (e.g., days 1–5) when sentiment is volatile; apply 1–3% downward bias to first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low cycles, model misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 7-day price to anchor forecast.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is flat, model often predicts minor drift; forecast should be within ±0.5% of 14-day moving average.
